source_references.count_basis: Fourteen unique source documents used: five primary or official records and nine independent reporting documents. Two primary records (SATS half-year results and MIDA's 9M investment release) predate the coverage window and are used only as background verification, not as new developments.
source_references.verification_note: S&P's official ratings-actions listing confirms NVIDIA's AA CreditWatch Negative status; Reuters supplies the rating rationale and Moody's response. ABS figures are checked against its release and detailed dataset. SATS operating figures and MIDA approved-investment figures are checked against primary company/government documents. Allegations and anonymous-source claims are attributed and not treated as established findings. AP's post-close report independently corroborates the US market closing figures and provides additional observations for Microsoft, Meta and SK hynix.

notes: The routine 72-hour publication interval from the 2026-11-25 routine update had not elapsed. This is an interim publication justified by NVIDIA's new S&P CreditWatch Negative action and the unusually broad AI-market repricing.
S&P did not downgrade NVIDIA in this window. Its AA rating remained on CreditWatch with negative implications; Reuters reported that a possible downgrade could be limited to one notch within 90 days.
Moody's Aa1 rating and stable outlook remained unchanged. Its stated view on near-term leadership uncertainty differs in emphasis from S&P's governance review.

Reuters' reporting on US intelligence assessments relies on people familiar with classified briefings. The FBI and CIA assessments described in the article are not public agency findings, and the article does not establish espionage or wrongdoing.
TIME's corporate-ownership investigation describes historical links involving Megaspeed's former parent. It does not establish current Chinese state ownership, current control, or unlawful conduct.
The Nasdaq-100's approach to a 20% drawdown was intraday. It closed down 0.6%; the report does not label the index as having closed in a bear market.

ABS's information-media-and-telecommunications capex category is broader than data centres. ABS attributed the sharp increase in part to server racks and data-centre processing equipment; the sector figure is not a pure data-centre spending total.

SATS is a diversified aviation-services company. Its cargo growth is not wholly attributable to AI shipments, and its operating-margin and cash-flow data are included to avoid equating volume growth with shareholder returns.

MIDA's RM123.5 billion figure is approved investment across proposed data-centre and cloud projects, not cash already deployed. A claim that up to half of future Southeast Asian capacity may not proceed is a single anonymous-source estimate reported by The Straits Times and is not used as a base case.

The Talkie app removal is reported by Reuters after media allegations about inappropriate interactions with minors. Apple and MiniMax did not immediately respond; the allegations are not presented as adjudicated findings. MiniMax's reported 2024 revenue concentration is historical, and its current chatbot revenue mix is not disclosed.
No timestamp-aligned valuation dataset was assembled. No price targets or personalised buy/sell recommendations are provided.
No new operating or earnings announcement was verified for most of the named priority companies during this exact window.
